preamble: Nasalization of the voiced palatal stop [ɟ] to the palatal nasal [ɲ] occurs in Jê languages of Brazil, where voiced stops and nasals form a single series whose nasality is determined by the syllable nucleus. In Proto-Northern Jê the voiced palatal stop */ɟ/ was realized as [ɲ] before nasal vowels (and as [ɟ] or [j] before oral ones), which is visible in palatalized nonfinite verb forms; Kaingang (Southern Jê), analysed with a voiced-stop series /b d ɟ ɡ/, realizes /ɟ/ as a full nasal [ɲ] between nasal vowels or word-initially before a nasal vowel.

examples.from: nonfinite palatal onset */ɟ/ before an oral vowel: *ga 'to roast' > nonfinite *ĵər [ɟ]
examples.to: before a nasal vowel: *ŋõr 'to sleep' > nonfinite *ñõt [ɲ], *ŋõ 'to give' > nonfinite *ñõr [ɲ]
examples.note: The palatalized onset of nonfinite verbs is the single phoneme */ɟ/, realized nasal [ɲ] before nasal nuclei, oral [ɟ] in stressed oral syllables and [j] in unstressed oral syllables.
Between nasal vowels the palatal of the voiced-stop series surfaces as a full nasal [ɲ]; between oral vowels it is an oral [ɟ] and word-initially before an oral vowel a prenasalized [ᶮɟ].

sources: Nikulin, A., & Salanova, A. P. (2019). Northern Jê Verb Morphology and the Reconstruction of Finiteness Alternations. International Journal of American Linguistics 85(4), 533-567. https://doi.org/10.1086/704565
